title: Customs Authority Enforcement and Regulatory Oversight
summary: The role of the Customs Authority has evolved from a traditional enforcement and assessment body under the Customs Act 1969 to a modern, technology-driven facilitator of trade. Recent instruments emphasize digital integration, risk-based management, and inter-agency coordination for transit and transshipment, while maintaining strict punitive powers for non-compliance.

evolution.operational_model: Shift from manual oversight to automated, risk-based, and digital-first customs procedures.
evolution.institutional_scope: Expanded to include inter-agency coordination and management of specialized programs like AEO and transit logistics.
evolution.enforcement_mechanism: Increased reliance on electronic tracking, digital audit trails, and ex-post facto regulatory oversight.

timeline.change: Introduction of digital system access (ESPIN), AEO program management, and mandatory electronic record-keeping for express services.
Formalization of inter-agency coordination, electronic sealing, and risk-based physical examination protocols for transit goods.

Express Service Provider: Express service providers are prohibited from transferring consignments to third parties or other express services for warehousing purposes, whether partially or in full.
They are required to maintain all import and export documentation according to legal provisions and must grant customs officers necessary access to these records.
Providers must notify customers promptly after consignment landing, including detailed information such as arrival date, time, clearance procedures, and other relevant data.
Goods must be delivered only after verifying the identity of the customer or their authorized representative.
They must maintain specific staff, office equipment, and information technology systems to ensure internal security, logistics, tracking, and expedited clearance.
They have a mandatory duty to immediately report any suspected smuggling, duty evasion, or violations of import-export compliance to the appropriate customs official.
Customs Authority: Customs officials are entitled to receive full access to records maintained by express service providers and must be informed immediately of any suspected regulatory violations or customs offences.

member_objects.clause_title: কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমের মাধ্যমে কার্য পরিচালনার জন্য ইউজার আইডি, পাসওয়ার্ড ও এজেন্ট নম্বর প্রদান

Customs Authority: The Customs Authority is responsible for issuing user IDs, passwords, and the Express Service Providers Identification Number (ESPIN) to licensees for performing customs procedures electronically.
The authority must verify that licensees meet the required infrastructure, equipment, and staffing standards before issuing access credentials to the customs computer system.

The authority has the power to suspend or deactivate a licensee's system access credentials and ESPIN without prior notice if the licensee fails to meet operational requirements, commits misconduct, or engages in smuggling and tax evasion.
Express Service Providers Identification: Licensees must obtain an ESPIN from the Customs Authority to process cargo declarations, customs clearance, duty payments, and delivery tracking within the customs computer system.
Automated System: Licensees are required to maintain an automated system capable of connecting to the customs gateway, which must include features for electronic cargo declaration, non-intrusive scanning, real-time tracking, data synchronization, and automated issuance of release notices.

The automated system must support electronic duty payments, automated invoice generation, maintenance of sender and recipient data, and customer-facing portals for shipment tracking and electronic notification of cargo arrival.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This system serves as the central platform for managing the lifecycle of imported consignments, including declaration, valuation, payment of duties and taxes, and delivery to the customer.

member_objects.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) এর প্রাপ্ত সুবিধা

Authorized Economic Operator: Authorized Economic Operators are categorized into three distinct classes, each receiving graduated levels of trade facilitation and customs privileges based on their compliance status.

Class 1 operators receive core benefits such as priority scanning, fast-track assessment, reduced physical examinations, and simplified clearance procedures, including the ability to utilize green lane processing for a portion of their declarations.

Class 2 operators receive all Class 1 benefits plus enhanced facilitation, including deferred duty and tax payment cycles, further reduced physical examination requirements, and access to internal management information systems.

Class 3 operators receive the highest tier of facilitation, including the most significant reductions in physical examination selection, extended deferred payment privileges, and the ability to conduct physical inspections at their own premises with official authorization.

Logistics operators recognized as Authorized Economic Operators receive specific operational benefits including priority in investigations, the right to use specialized accreditation logos, and the ability to provide consolidated guarantees for transit and transshipment cargo.
Customs Authority: The Customs Authority manages the Authorized Economic Operator program, including the right to subject 100% of shipments to physical examination if irregularities are detected, overriding standard facilitation thresholds.
The Customs Authority provides informal guidance via email to Authorized Economic Operators, though such advice does not create legal binding obligations or establish rights for clearance purposes.
The Customs Authority facilitates trade by providing special identification for representatives of Authorized Economic Operators, enabling easier access to and operations within customs stations.
Mutual Recognition Agreement: Class 2 and Class 3 Authorized Economic Operators may benefit from special privileges when exporting to foreign countries where a formal mutual recognition agreement is in place between Bangladesh and the partner nation.

Authorized Economic Operator: The recognition of an Authorized Economic Operator may be suspended or cancelled by the Director General of the Center based on various grounds, including submission of false information, involvement in smuggling, duty evasion, or misuse of concessional facilities.

When an Authorized Economic Operator status is suspended or cancelled, all associated privileges are also revoked, although audit actions or legal proceedings regarding previously cleared goods may still continue.

If recognition is cancelled due to specific offenses like document falsification or smuggling, the entity is prohibited from applying for new recognition for a period of several years from the date of cancellation.
Director General of the Center: The Director General has the authority to immediately suspend the recognition certificate of an Authorized Economic Operator upon the discovery of specific irregularities or credible evidence of misconduct.
The Director General is responsible for issuing a show-cause notice to the affected entity within a set timeframe after the initial suspension of their recognition certificate.

Following the consideration of a show-cause response or the expiry of the response period, the Director General prepares recommendations regarding the permanent cancellation, downgrading, or reinstatement of the recognition status for submission to the relevant committee.
Customs Authority: The Customs Authority is responsible for providing information to the Center regarding any irregularities, tax evasion, or smuggling activities discovered within its jurisdiction involving an Authorized Economic Operator.
Authorized Economic Operator Recognition: The committee is responsible for reviewing the recommendations provided by the Director General to make final decisions on the permanent cancellation, class downgrading, or reinstatement of the Authorized Economic Operator certificate.

member_objects.clause_title: অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর (AEO) হিসাবে আবেদনের যোগ্যতা

Authorized Economic Operator: Eligibility for Authorized Economic Operator status is limited to persons or entities directly involved in the international supply chain, such as exporters, importers, or logistics operators.
Applicants must be well-established in Bangladesh, have at least four years of business experience, and meet specific minimum capital and annual turnover thresholds.

Financial and operational integrity is mandatory, requiring applicants to maintain clean records regarding tax and customs compliance, and possess robust electronic systems for record-keeping and customs auditing.

Authorized Economic Operator status is granted to the entire organization, not individual departments or branches, and requires comprehensive security, administrative, and financial transparency protocols to be strictly maintained.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: Applicants for Authorized Economic Operator status must fulfill all relevant qualifications outlined in the Self-Assessment Questionnaire.
Electronic Cargo Tracking System: Businesses must maintain standards for using electronic seals for cargo security, ensuring that only authorized personnel can handle or examine these seals.
National Board of Revenue: Applicants must maintain business data and accounts using software approved by the National Board of Revenue, ensuring customs authorities have the necessary access for verification and monitoring.
Customs Authority: Applicants must provide immediate notification to customs authorities regarding any disruptions to regulatory compliance or security breaches within their business operations.
Partnership Act 1932: Partnership firms must provide valid registration certificates from the relevant registrar to prove their legal status when applying for Authorized Economic Operator recognition.

(২) সংশ্লিষ্ট চুক্তি বা প্রটোকল বা স্ট্যান্ডার্ড অপারেটিং প্রসিডিউর এ উল্লিখিত কাস্টমস বন্ড বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টি বা অঙ্গীকারনামা সংশ্লিষ্ট ক্ষেত্রে বৈধ গ্যারান্টি হিসেবে বিবেচিত হইবে।
(৩) ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট প্রক্রিয়া সম্পন্ন হওয়ার পরবর্তী ৭ (সাত) কার্য দিবসের মধ্যে ক্ষেত্রমত, কাস্টমস বন্ড বা অঙ্গীকারনামা বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টির অবমুক্তি নিশ্চিত করিতে হইবে।
(৪) আইনের বিধান অনুসরণপূর্বক একই অনুমোদিত ব্যক্তি বা এজেন্ট কর্তৃক একাধিক ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট কার্যক্রম সম্পাদনের ক্ষেত্রে সমন্বিত গ্যারান্টি দাখিলের সুযোগ প্রদান করা যাইবে।
(৫) সন্তোষজনক কার্যক্রম পরিপালনের রেকর্ড রহিয়াছে এবং পূর্ববর্তী বৎসরে অনূ্যন ২০ (বিশ) টি ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট চালান ব্যবস্থাপনায় অংশগ্রহণ করিয়াছে এইরূপ কোনো অনুমোদিত ব্যক্তি যদি অভ্যন্তরীণ প্রবেশ বন্দর সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস কমিশনারের নিকট আবেদন করেন, তাহা হইলে তাহাকে সমন্বিত গ্যারান্টি প্রদানকারী হিসাবে অনুমোদন প্রদান করা যাইবে।
(৬) কাস্টমস বন্ড বা অঙ্গীকারনামা বা লেটার অব গ্যারান্টি সম্পর্কিত সকল বিধান কাস্টমস ওয়েবসাইট এবং ইন্টারনেটের মাধ্যমে সকলের জন্য সহজলভ্য করিতে হইবে।

Transit and Transshipment: Each transit or transshipment shipment requires an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee from a scheduled bank in Bangladesh for an amount equivalent to the applicable duties and taxes to mitigate revenue risks and prevent irregularities.
Customs bonds, letters of guarantee, or undertakings as specified in relevant agreements, protocols, or standard operating procedures are recognized as valid forms of security.
Customs authorities must ensure the release of bonds or guarantees within a specified number of working days after the completion of the transit or transshipment process.
Authorized agents or persons may submit a consolidated guarantee for multiple transit or transshipment activities in accordance with legal provisions.

Qualified persons who have a record of satisfactory compliance and have managed a minimum threshold of transit or transshipment shipments in the previous year may be approved for consolidated guarantee submission upon application to the customs commissioner.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is responsible for ensuring that all regulations and procedures regarding bonds, letters of guarantee, and undertakings are made easily accessible to the public through the official customs website and the internet.

(২) কন্টেইনারজাত নহে এইরূপ পণ্যচালানের ক্ষেত্রে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেম কর্তৃক কার্গো ঘোষণায় (ম্যানিফেস্ট) প্রদত্ত তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে ঝুঁকি ব্যবস্থাপনার মাধ্যমে কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য পণ্যচালান নির্বাচন করিতে হইবে।
(৩) কোনো অভ্যন্তরীণ প্রবেশ বন্দর সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস অফিসে স্ক্যানার এবং এইরূপ কম্পিউটার প্রোগ্রাম নির্ভর ঝুঁকি ব্যবস্থাপনা পদ্ধতি কার্যকর না থাকিলে দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা উচ্চ ঝুঁকির ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট পণ্যচালনাসমূহ কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য নির্বাচন করিবেন।
(৪) কন্টেইনারজাত নহে এইরূপ পণ্যচালানের ক্ষেত্রে কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য নির্ধারিত পণ্যচালানের সংখ্যা শতকরা ৫ (পাঁচ) ভাগ এর অধিক হইবে না।
(৫) কাস্টমস কমিশনার বা সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের দায়িত্বপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা যুক্তিসঙ্গত মনে করিলে দৈবচয়নের ভিত্তিতে পণ্যচালান নির্বাচনপূর্বক কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য নির্দেশনা প্রদান করিতে পারিবে।
(৬) গোয়েন্দা তথ্যের ভিত্তিতে যে কোনো পণ্যচালান কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য নির্বাচন করা যাইবে।
(৭) কোনো ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট পণ্যচালান কায়িক পরীক্ষার জন্য নির্বাচিত হইলে অগ্রাধিকারের ভিত্তিতে ঐ পণ্যচালানের কায়িক পরীক্ষা সম্পাদন করিতে হইবে।

Transit and Transshipment: This clause outlines the inspection protocols for cargo under transit or transshipment, mandating scanning for containerized goods at ports of entry, with physical examination required if scanning raises suspicions. For non-containerized goods, selection for physical inspection is determined through risk management systems or discretionary authority, subject to specific percentage limits and prioritization requirements.
Customs Authority: The customs office at the port of entry is responsible for conducting cargo scanning and executing physical examinations based on risk management or intelligence. Officials have the authority to select shipments for physical inspection, even in the absence of automated scanning or risk assessment systems, to ensure compliance during transit or transshipment.
Risk Management System: The Customs computer system uses a risk management approach to select non-containerized cargo for physical examination based on declarations made in the manifest. Where such automated systems are unavailable, authorized officers are empowered to manually identify high-risk shipments for examination.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or the officer in charge of a station has the discretionary authority to order the physical inspection of cargo through a random selection process if deemed reasonable.

(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এ উল্লিখিত ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ব্যবহারের ক্ষেত্রে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড কর্তৃক জারীকৃত এতদসংক্রান্ত বিধিমালা যথাযথভাবে অনুসরণ করিতে হইবে।

(৪) ইলেকট্রনিক সিল ও লক সেবা প্রদানের লক্ষ্যে প্রতিষ্ঠান নিযুক্তকরণসহ আনুষঙ্গিক কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন না হওয়া পর্যন্ত ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট পণ্যচালান বাংলাদেশের প্রবেশ বন্দর হইতে প্রস্থান বন্দর পর্যন্ত পরিবহনকালীন প্রবেশ বন্দরের কাস্টমস কর্তৃপক্ষ এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস, এক্সাইজ ও ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট কর্তৃক প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক কাস্টমস এসকর্ট কর্মকর্তা নিয়োগ করিতে হইবে।

Transit and Transshipment: All containers, tankers, covered vans, or enclosed ship holds carrying transit or transshipment goods must be secured with electronic seals and locks equipped with GPS trackers to ensure security and proper customs control.

Until a system for electronic seal and lock service providers is fully implemented, goods must be transported under the supervision of customs escort officers appointed by the entry port customs authorities and the relevant Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate.
Electronic seals and locks must be removed from vehicles carrying transit or transshipment goods before they depart from the relevant internal customs exit port.
National Board of Revenue: The use of electronic seals for transit or transshipment goods must strictly adhere to the regulations issued by the National Board of Revenue.
Customs Authority: Customs authorities at the port of entry are responsible for coordinating the appointment of escort officers to monitor transit or transshipment goods until electronic security systems are fully operational.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১৫। আন্তঃসংস্থা সমন্বয়।—ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট পণ্য ছাড়করণ প্রক্রিয়া সহজীকরণের উদ্দেশ্যে এবং কার্যকর নিয়ন্ত্রণ প্রতিষ্ঠার লক্ষ্যে কর্মদিবস ও কর্মঘণ্টা, কর্মপদ্ধতি এবং স্থাপনা ব্যবহারের ক্ষেত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট সংস্থাসমূহের মধ্যে সমন্বয় সাধনের দায়িত্ব বাংলাদেশের প্রবেশ বন্দর ও প্রস্থান বন্দর সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস কর্তৃপক্ষ পালন করিবে।

Transit and Transshipment: The customs authorities at entry and exit ports are responsible for coordinating with other relevant agencies to simplify the customs clearance process for goods under transit or transshipment.
Customs Authority: Customs authorities at entry and exit ports are tasked with ensuring inter-agency coordination regarding working days, operational hours, procedures, and infrastructure usage to improve regulatory control and trade facilitation.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১৬। জাতীয় ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট সমন্বয়কারী নিয়োগ।—ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট সম্পর্কিত সকল প্রশ্নাবলী ও প্রস্তাব নিষ্পত্তিকরণ এবং সংশ্লিষ্ট অন্যান্য সকল সংস্থার সহিত সমন্বয় সাধনের উদ্দেশ্যে বোর্ড একজন কাস্টমস কমিশনারকে জাতীয় ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট সমন্বয়কারী হিসেবে নিয়োগ করিবে এবং সকল ট্রানজিট বা ট্রান্সশিপমেন্ট এর ক্ষেত্রে বাংলাদেশের প্রবেশ বন্দর ও প্রস্থান বন্দরের একজন করিয়া কর্মকর্তা প্রদান সমন্বয়কারীকে সহায়তা প্রদান করিবে।

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to appoint a Commissioner of Customs to serve as the National Transit or Transshipment Coordinator.
Transit and Transshipment: The Transit or Transshipment Coordinator is responsible for resolving all queries and proposals related to transit or transshipment activities and ensuring coordination with relevant government agencies.
Commissioner of Customs: A Commissioner of Customs is designated as the National Transit or Transshipment Coordinator to oversee and harmonize transit and transshipment operations.
Customs Authority: Designated officials at both entry and exit ports are required to assist the National Transit or Transshipment Coordinator in managing transit and transshipment logistics.

Provisional Assessment of Customs Duty: This clause provides the legal basis for the provisional assessment of goods when an immediate final assessment is not possible due to the need for chemical analysis, further investigation, or incomplete documentation.

Provisional assessment can be ordered by a customs officer of the rank of Assistant Commissioner or higher upon the provision of security or a bank guarantee by the importer or exporter for the potential difference in duty.

Final assessment must be completed within a specified number of working days from the date of provisional assessment, or from the date of final resolution if the matter is sub-judice before a court or tribunal.

Following final assessment, the customs authority is required to adjust the paid or guaranteed amount against the actual duty payable, with the importer or exporter either paying the balance or receiving a refund.

82A. Procedure in case of goods not assessed or out-passed by Customs after presentation of the related bill of entry within a specified period.- If any goods, other than goods detained, seized, confiscated, under adjudication or appeal under the provisions of this Act, for which a bill of entry has duly been presented, are not assessed and out-passed within seven working days the owner of such goods may serve a notice upon the Commissioner to finalize the Customs formalities within three working days enabling him to pay duty and taxes and clear the goods, and the said Commissioner or any officer authorized on his behalf shall do so, if the import is in order, or issue a show cause notice if the import is not in order.
Explanation.- For the purpose of this section "detained goods" include goods detained for chemical examination, radiation test, reference for resolution disputes on of classification, value, ITC aspect or any other legal disputes.]

Bill of Entry: This entity represents the document presented to Customs for the clearance of imported goods.
The submission of a bill of entry initiates the customs assessment process and triggers the timeline for the finalization of customs formalities.
Detained Goods: These are goods held by customs authorities for specific reasons such as chemical examination, radiation testing, or disputes regarding classification, valuation, and import policy requirements.
Detained goods are explicitly excluded from the simplified procedure for clearance when assessment or out-passing is delayed beyond the specified time frame.
Seized Goods: These goods are excluded from the expedited clearance procedure applicable to goods awaiting assessment or out-passing.
Confiscated Goods: These goods are excluded from the expedited clearance procedure applicable to goods awaiting assessment or out-passing.
Adjudication of Customs Cases: Goods subject to pending adjudication under the provisions of the Customs Act are ineligible for the fast-track clearance notice process defined for delayed assessments.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is responsible for finalizing customs formalities within a set time frame upon receiving a notice from the goods owner.
If the import formalities are not in order, the Commissioner or authorized officer must issue a show cause notice to the importer.
Show Cause Notice: This legal instrument is issued by the Commissioner of Customs when the import documentation or status is found to be non-compliant or not in order.
Customs Clearance Procedure: A procedural framework is established to ensure goods are assessed and out-passed within a specific period after the submission of the bill of entry.
When delays occur, owners of goods may invoke a notice procedure to compel the customs authority to complete assessment or provide a formal explanation for non-compliance.

To initiate a transfer, the owner must apply to the appropriate customs authority by following the prescribed form and providing the required details about the goods and the destination customs station.
Warehousing Station: A warehousing station acts as a site where goods are stored under bond, and the law provides a legal mechanism for moving goods from one such station to another.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond), or another authorized Commissioner of Customs, is the designated authority responsible for reviewing and processing applications submitted by owners for the transfer of goods between warehousing stations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to prescribe the specific forms, procedures, and conditions that owners must follow when applying to transfer warehoused goods between different stations.

The officer has the authority to permit the clearance of coastal goods if they are satisfied that the goods are correctly entered in the submitted bills.
Bill of Coastal Goods: These documents are required to be carried on the vessel and presented to the appropriate officer at the destination port to facilitate the legal unloading and clearance of the goods.

Customs Act 1969: The Act establishes the legal framework for resolving disputes, including the initiation of the Alternative Dispute Resolution process.

Importer: An importer involved in a dispute with customs authorities is eligible to apply for the resolution of their case through the Alternative Dispute Resolution process.
Exporter: An exporter involved in a dispute with customs authorities is eligible to apply for the resolution of their case through the Alternative Dispute Resolution process.
Pre-shipment Inspection Agency: Pre-shipment inspection agencies are entitled to utilize the Alternative Dispute Resolution process to settle disputes related to their activities.

Customs and Value Added Tax Appellate Au: Disputes pending or related to these appellate authorities may be diverted to the Alternative Dispute Resolution process in accordance with the Act.

Alternative Dispute Resolution: This mechanism is established to resolve disputes regarding customs levy, assessment, classification, collection, refund of duties, and the imposition of fines or penalties.
It provides a structured process for handling disagreements involving customs assessment and valuation that are pending before customs authorities, appellate authorities, or courts of law.
Customs Authority: These are the administrative bodies responsible for handling customs-related cases, including those subject to Alternative Dispute Resolution.
Customs Valuation: Disputes concerning the determination of value for assessment purposes fall under the scope of Alternative Dispute Resolution, subject to the relevant subsections of the Customs Act.
Bill of Entry: Disputes arising from the submission of this document or related Demand Notices and Show Cause Notices are eligible for Alternative Dispute Resolution, provided they do not involve excluded criminal or fraudulent categories.
Bill of Export: Disputes arising from the submission of this document or related Demand Notices and Show Cause Notices are eligible for Alternative Dispute Resolution, provided they do not involve excluded criminal or fraudulent categories.
Show Cause Notice: This instrument is recognized as a basis for disputes eligible for Alternative Dispute Resolution when issued in relation to import or export declarations.
Pre-shipment Inspection Agency: Pending disputes related to penalties imposed on these agencies are eligible for consideration under Alternative Dispute Resolution.
Prohibited Goods: Disputes involving the seizure and confiscation of these items are explicitly excluded from the scope of Alternative Dispute Resolution.
Smuggled Goods: Disputes involving the seizure and confiscation of these items are explicitly excluded from the scope of Alternative Dispute Resolution.
Bonded Warehouse: Disputes arising from violations of licensing or bond-related conditions are excluded from the scope of Alternative Dispute Resolution.

Customs Act 1969: The Third Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 outlines the scope for making rules regarding customs procedures, including the seizure and forfeiture of prohibited goods, duty drawbacks, and administrative mechanisms for customs clearance.
It empowers the relevant authorities to regulate customs operations, assess goods, manage transit and transshipment, control bonded warehouses, and oversee licensing requirements for customs agents.

The schedule provides the foundational authority for framing rules on passenger baggage, postal imports/exports, coastal trade controls, and various operational directives to ensure the effective implementation of customs law.
Prohibited Goods: The schedule provides for procedures related to the seizure and forfeiture of goods imported or intended for export that are classified as prohibited.

These procedures cover the verification of information, notice requirements to owners, custody or release of goods under security, and the adjudication of claims or damages arising from false information.
Duty Drawback: Provisions are established for granting refunds of customs duties on goods produced, processed, or repaired for subsequent export, as well as on materials used in such manufacturing.
The regulatory framework covers conditions for claiming drawbacks, time limits for export and filing claims, and the authority to prohibit drawbacks for specific classes of goods.
Customs Valuation: The schedule authorizes the development of rules for the assessment of imported or exported goods.

It mandates that importers and exporters submit necessary information, present relevant books and documents, and disclose the nature and source of funds used for acquisitions to ensure accurate valuation.
Transit and Transshipment: Rules are specified for the movement, sealing, and control of goods in transit or transshipment, including movements through foreign territories to reach parts of Bangladesh.
This includes the authority to impose conditions or prohibitions, set fees, and define the powers of customs officers regarding the handling and security of such goods.
Customs Agent: The framework defines the licensing process for customs agents, including eligibility criteria, license duration, and required security deposits.
It establishes the authority to grant, suspend, or cancel licenses and provides a mechanism for appealing such administrative actions, as well as defining rules for the conduct of business.
Passenger Baggage: The schedule provides for the regulation of passenger and crew baggage, including its definition, declaration, examination, and clearance processes.
It outlines conditions under which specific classes of baggage or goods may be exempted from customs duties and establishes the limits for such exemptions.
Customs Authority: The schedule grants customs authorities the power to inspect factories or buildings, verify accounts, enforce vessel clearances, and perform chemical testing on substances like spirits.
It also authorizes the imposition of penalties, the requirement of manifests, and the issuance of special passes to ensure compliance with customs regulations.
Coastal Trade: Regulations allow for the control of coastal trade to prevent the illegal removal of duty-paid or prohibited goods from Bangladesh.
This includes mechanisms to prevent the unauthorized substitution of cargo on ships and the ability to restrict the movement of specific classes of goods between designated ports.
Bonded Warehouse: The schedule encompasses rules for the management of bonded warehouses, including operations performed within the warehouse and cost-recovery for accompanying customs officers.
It also addresses fees payable by owners for the administration and distribution of goods stored under customs supervision.

Business Identification Number: The Business Identification Number is required for importers and exporters when submitting customs declarations for the clearance of goods.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is the authority responsible for the assessment of duties, taxes, and other charges on imported or exported goods.
The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to permit the release of goods under an unconditional and continuous bank guarantee in lieu of immediate payment of customs revenue.
The Commissioner of Customs is empowered to demand encashment of a bank guarantee and initiate legal proceedings against the bank if the institution fails to honor the guarantee upon request.
Bank Guarantee: A bank guarantee serves as an unconditional and continuous financial security instrument submitted by a bank on behalf of an importer or exporter to facilitate customs clearance without immediate payment of duties and taxes.

The bank issuing the guarantee is contractually obligated to pay the specified customs revenue to the Commissioner of Customs upon demand without needing prior consultation with the importer or exporter.
Failure by a bank to encash a guarantee upon request by the customs authority makes the bank liable for legal action by the customs authorities.
